topIssues.title: fix(ci): fence Calendar typecheck behind Video declarations
topIssues.author: NubsCarson
topIssues.body:
# Problem

A clean GitHub runner can start `@elizaos/plugin-calendar#typecheck` while `@elizaos/plugin-video#build` has emitted `dist/index.js` but not `dist/index.d.ts`. Calendar currently traverses `@elizaos/agent` source, whose generated optional-plugin map imports Video, so TypeScript fails nondeterministically with TS7016.

# Scope

Add the missing package-specific Turbo ordering edge for Calendar typecheck. Do not add a Calendar to Video manifest dependency, suppress TS7016, or rely on retries. Remove the temporary edge in the later canonical Calendar slice after that slice eliminates the Calendar to Agent source coupling.

# Acceptance

- [ ] A clean workspace schedules Video build before Calendar typecheck.
- [ ] The exact affected typecheck command passes from a clean install.
- [ ] Turbo dependency audits and full repository verification pass.
- [ ] The final cumulative approved product tree remains unchanged after the canonical Calendar slice removes the now-unneeded edge.

# Reproduction

GitHub run 30956924035, job 92152052372: Calendar typecheck began before Video declaration generation completed and failed at `packages/agent/src/runtime/optional-plugin-imports.generated.ts`.

topIssues.author: 0xSolace
topIssues.body:

- AI assistance: yes
- AI provider/model: openai-codex / gpt-5.6-sol

- Contribution skill revision: elizaOS/eliza@e37924817dd457f3c5cc1547531c7054336a3740:packages/skills/skills/contribute-to-eliza
- Attribution status: self-reported

## Scope

The contributor skill requires `live-report.mjs` before work selection, but its GitHub adapter invokes `gh api --slurp`. Ubuntu 24.04 currently packages GitHub CLI 2.45.0, whose `gh api` does not support `--slurp`, so the mandatory inventory exits before making its first read. The same compatibility gap was reproduced in two independent contributor-skill audits.

Replace the `--slurp` dependency with a pagination format supported by the repository's practical GitHub CLI baseline while preserving the adapter's GET-only and complete-pagination guarantees. Document the compatibility contract in the skill and keep malformed or partial output fail-closed. This scope must not edit workflows.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] `live-report.mjs --repo elizaOS/eliza --json` completes with GitHub CLI 2.45.0.
- [ ] Every paginated request remains explicitly `--method GET`; no mutation verb can enter the adapter.
- [ ] Multi-page arrays are returned completely and in order, including empty-page and malformed-output handling.
- [ ] Spawn failures, nonzero exits, malformed records, and truncated output fail with actionable endpoint context.
- [ ] Deterministic tests cover success, multiple pages, empty results, malformed/truncated output, command failure, and GET-only invocation.
- [ ] The skill documents the supported pagination behavior without claiming an unsupported minimum GitHub CLI version.
- [ ] The real read-only inventory is run, its JSON opens successfully, and summary/candidate excerpts are manually inspected.

## Evidence Plan

- [ ] Screenshots or recording: N/A - CLI compatibility change has no rendered UI.
- [ ] Logs: attach the pre-fix unsupported-flag failure and post-fix live inventory transcript inline.
- [ ] Real-LLM trajectories: N/A - no model, prompt, provider, action, or agent runtime behavior changes.
- [ ] Domain artifacts: attach the post-fix machine-readable inventory summary and manually reviewed candidate excerpt.
- [ ] CI or local commands: focused contribution-skill tests, package build/typecheck/lint, repository `bun run verify`, and live `--json` inventory.

## Claim / Status Notes

Unclaimed at filing. No active product Project applies to this repository-infrastructure scope; ownership will be recorded by the required public claim comment and branch.

topIssues.title: Dependabot uv branches fail trusted PR normalization
topIssues.author: lalalune
topIssues.body:
The PR normalization workflow accepts Dependabot npm, GitHub Actions, and pip branch prefixes but rejects the `dependabot/uv/*` prefix generated by the configured pip ecosystem. This makes uv-group PRs fail normalization before evidence validation and blocks the aggregate Develop PR Gate.

Add the uv prefix to the exact first-party allowlist and extend the policy test so every configured pip branch form remains trusted without broadening actor or repository checks.

topIssues.title: fix(ui): align chat-sheet transcription privacy-stop contract
topIssues.author: lalalune
topIssues.body:
## Problem

The `Chat shell gestures` workflow is deterministically red on `develop`. Production and the component unit contract intentionally expose both transcription-only Stop and a master `stop transcription and mic` privacy control while a reply is in flight, but the browser E2E still asserts that the master mic is absent.

This stale semantic merge result has failed on consecutive develop heads and hides regressions in the master stop path.

## Acceptance criteria

- Require the master mic control during in-flight transcription.
- Verify its accessible label and enabled state.
- Exercise the control through the real Chromium fixture and prove the controller callback fires.
- Verify capture controls disappear and generation Stop takes ownership afterward.
- Keep all existing chat-sheet gesture and console checks green.

Related workflow run: https://github.com/elizaOS/eliza/actions/runs/30604753986.

topPRs.title: fix(core): detect LifeOps plugin to drive passive-connector default
topPRs.author: odilitime
topPRs.body:
# Relates to

Fixes a silent bug where standalone elizaOS agents (no LifeOps) would never reply on Discord, Telegram, iMessage, Signal, WhatsApp, or Matrix because `lifeOpsPassiveConnectorsEnabled()` defaulted to `true` even when `plugin-personal-assistant` was not loaded.

- [x] This PR targets `develop` and is rebased onto the latest `origin/develop` with zero conflicts.
- [x] `bun test packages/core/src/__tests__/lifeops-passive-connectors.test.ts` passes (15/15, 100% coverage).
- [x] A reviewer can confirm the change works without reading the code, from the evidence attached below.

# Sync with develop

- [x] Rebased/merged onto the latest `origin/develop`; zero conflicts.
- [x] `bun run verify` — lint and typecheck pass on changed files; two pre-existing Biome errors in unrelated payment/messaging test files are not introduced by this PR.

# Risks

Low. The change only affects the **default** fallback path — agents that already set `ELIZA_LIFEOPS_PASSIVE_CONNECTORS=false` (or `=true`) are unaffected because explicit settings continue to win. LifeOps agents that load `plugin-personal-assistant` continue to get passive mode automatically. Standalone agents that don't load that plugin now correctly default to active-reply mode.

# Background

## What does this PR do?

`lifeOpsPassiveConnectorsEnabled()` in `packages/core/src/lifeops-passive-connectors.ts` used to return `true` by default when no env var was set. Every connector (Discord, Telegram, iMessage, Signal, WhatsApp, Matrix) gates auto-reply on this function, so any agent without `ELIZA_LIFEOPS_PASSIVE_CONNECTORS=false` in its `.env` would silently ingest messages into memory and never generate a reply.

The fix adds plugin-presence detection as the new fallback:

**Priority order (unchanged for explicit settings):**
1. Runtime setting via `getSetting(...)` — always wins
2. `ELIZA_LIFEOPS_PASSIVE_CONNECTORS` / `LIFEOPS_PASSIVE_CONNECTORS` env var — wins over detection
3. **New:** whether `@elizaos/plugin-personal-assistant` is in `runtime.plugins` — passive on if loaded, passive off otherwise

`SettingsReader` gains an optional `plugins?: Array<{ name: string }>` field — structurally compatible with `IAgentRuntime.plugins: Plugin[]` and all existing connector call sites that pass `this.runtime`.

## What kind of change is this?

Bug fix — behaviour change only in the default (no env var) path for agents not loading the LifeOps plugin.

# Documentation changes needed?

No. The env var `ELIZA_LIFEOPS_PASSIVE_CONNECTORS=false` workaround documented in some deployment guides still works and can be removed at operators' convenience, but is not required.

# Testing

## Where should a reviewer start?

`packages/core/src/lifeops-passive-connectors.ts` — the diff is 25 lines. Then `packages/core/src/__tests__/lifeops-passive-connectors.test.ts` for the new unit tests.

## Detailed testing steps

```bash
bun test packages/core/src/__tests__/lifeops-passive-connectors.test.ts
# 15 pass, 0 fail, 100% line + function coverage
```

To verify end-to-end: boot an elizaOS agent **without** `plugin-personal-assistant` and without any `ELIZA_LIFEOPS_PASSIVE_CONNECTORS` env var. Previously it would silently ingest Discord messages; after this fix it generates replies as expected.

# Evidence Gate

- [x] Before/after screenshots — `N/A - no UI surface changes; pure logic fix in a core utility function`
- [x] Walkthrough video — `N/A - no user-visible flow changes`
- [x] Backend logs — `N/A - fix is in the passive-connector gate; no new runtime code path`
- [x] Frontend logs — `N/A - no frontend changes`
- [x] Real-LLM trajectory — `N/A - no model behaviour change`
- [x] Domain artifacts — `N/A - no DB, memory, wallet, or scheduled-task changes`

# Evidence Details

15 unit tests with 100% line + function coverage on the changed file, covering: default-off without plugin, default-on with plugin loaded, env var overrides (both keys, both directions), runtime setting overrides (string and boolean), and null/undefined runtime graceful handling.

## Known gaps / failures

None. Pre-existing Biome lint errors in `src/features/messaging/triage/__tests__/list-inbox-action.test.ts` and `src/features/payments/actions/payment.test.ts` are not introduced by this PR.

- Sends outbound media sequentially with reply/topic fidelity, MarkdownV2 captions, `sendVoice`, canonical sent-memory persistence, and visible unsupported-media failures.
- Splits long rich text against Telegram's final 4096 UTF-16-unit limit while preserving/reopening supported formatting constructs.

## What kind of change is this?

Feature, non-breaking connector fidelity improvement.

# Documentation changes needed?

- [ ] Full `bun run verify` was not run. Targeted verification is listed below.

# Risks

Medium. This adds a new outbound realtime provider and a production provider-selection seam. It is default-off. Cartesia remains the default and is the only fallback, limited to Fish transport/connect failure or first-audio timeout before any Fish audio byte. Fish is never replaced after first audio, preventing mixed voices.

# Background

## What does this PR do?

- adds `@elizaos/plugin-fish-audio`, default-off behind `ELIZA_TTS_FISH_ENABLED`, registered as `ModelType.TEXT_TO_SPEECH`
- implements Fish Audio's public realtime WebSocket API with MessagePack `start` / `text` / `stop` and streamed `audio` / `finish` frames
- supports configurable `s2.1` and `s2.1-pro`, emitting raw PCM16 mono 24 kHz matching the Cartesia downlink
- adds bounded pre-open queueing, first-audio metrics, and strict barge-in cancellation
- adds guarded Cartesia fallback before the first Fish audio byte only

## What kind of change is this?

Feature, non-breaking and flag-gated.

## Production path

The production TTS leg executes in `packages/cloud/api/v1/voice/session/lib/session.ts`. This is the `VoiceSession` path fed by incremental SSE deltas from `streamElizaConversation`. Provider selection and guarded fallback are wired there, not at a legacy plugin-only seam. Worker outbound WebSocket authorization is wired through `packages/cloud/api/v1/voice/session/lib/provider-socket-factory.ts`.

# Documentation changes needed?

Plugin configuration and the credential-gated live-test command are documented in `plugins/plugin-fish-audio/README.md`.

# Testing

## Where should a reviewer start?

1. `plugins/plugin-fish-audio/src/index.ts`
2. `packages/cloud/shared/src/lib/services/fish-audio-tts.ts`
3. `packages/cloud/api/v1/voice/session/lib/session.ts`
4. Their mocked-WebSocket tests

## Detailed testing steps

- `bun test packages/cloud/shared/src/lib/services/__tests__/fish-audio-tts.test.ts` (5 pass, 1 skipped pending key)
- `bun test packages/cloud/api/v1/voice/session/__tests__/ws-lifecycle.test.ts --test-name-pattern 'Fish|Cartesia as the default'` (6 pass)
- `bun test packages/cloud/api/v1/voice/session/__tests__/ws-route-upgrade.test.ts --test-name-pattern 'Fish realtime TTS'` (2 pass)
- `bun run --cwd plugins/plugin-fish-audio typecheck` (pass)
- `bun run --cwd plugins/plugin-fish-audio test` (4 pass, 1 skipped pending key)
- `bun run --cwd plugins/plugin-fish-audio build` (pass)
- `bun run --cwd packages/cloud/shared typecheck` (pass)
- `bun run --cwd packages/cloud/api typecheck` (pass, including Worker bundle check)
- `git diff --check` (pass)

Mock coverage proves exact MessagePack sequencing, first-audio latency emission, PCM downlink bytes, default-off selection, connect/timeout fallback, no fallback after first audio, provider-error behavior, backpressure, and abort/barge-in cancellation.
